Performers
Musopen Symphony (orchestra, as named on the Commons description) Disputed: sources disagree

The Commons description says Musopen Symphony; the embedded FLAC artist and albumartist, and the upstream Archive file entry, say Czech National Symphony Orchestra. A project-name/ensemble-name relationship is possible but not explicitly explained in the sources. No conductor is identified.

  • Musopen Symphony (orchestra)
  • Czech National Symphony Orchestra (orchestra)

Processing
The Commons FLAC master is 24-bit; the upstream collection description says 32-bit. Disputed: sources disagree

The file-specific metadata is used for digital.format: 48 kHz, stereo, libFLAC 1.2.1 20070917. The collection-wide 32-bit statement is retained as a conflicting source claim, not silently substituted for the file metadata. Restoration settings are unknown.

  • 24 bits per sample in the actual Commons FLAC metadata.
  • 32 bits per sample, as stated in the upstream collection description.

Composition rights
Public-domain original composition, as asserted by Commons. Documented

The musical-composition tag is PD-old-auto-expired, deathyear=1897. This does not license a later edition, arrangement or recording.

[1]
Recording rights
Rule 1 — recording release: PD-author public-domain dedication by Musopen. Documented

Commons explicitly applies PD-author by Musopen to the recording, separately from the composition. This is the programme’s explicit Musopen recording-release route, not an age-based inference or a claim that a Public Domain Mark is itself a licence. The session date is not needed for this route.

[6]

Musopen Symphony (Commons credit); Czech National Symphony Orchestra (embedded and upstream credit; attribution unresolved). Musopen Kickstarter Project / Internet Archive, via Wikimedia Commons. Public-domain dedication attributed to Musopen. Rights statement
